evidence: Reward formula: task tests/scoring.toml and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean; sha256 95f70d6e... / 13de2b38...). Gates render/constraints = 0.0 (no reward mass, all_pass binary), weights functional 0.6 > polish 0.2 + visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; score.py:52-59 zeroes reward unless every gate > 0 and functional > 0.05, else weighted mean. I imported the frozen score.py (python -B, temp dirs in scratchpad) and swept 216 gate/functional/polish/visual combinations: 0 cases where a component-wise-dominating score vector got a lower reward, so the aggregation itself cannot invert a ranking. Functional criteria weights (functional/judge.toml) sum to 44.0 as the header comment states (3+4+4+2+1.5+4+4+2+3+1.5+1.5+1.5+2.5+1.5+4+4) and follow the stated rule (core legal parts 2.0, chat 1.5, small 1.0); walls/retention/holds/persistence carry the most mass, matching the brief's 'two things matter more than anything else'. Craft cannot outweigh function: max polish+visual = 0.4 < 0.6 and polish rows (delete_confirm, link_highlight, transcript_print) themselves require working delete/search/transcript. Gates cannot fail a stronger app: render needs only reachability, no pre-sign-in leak, wrong-password refusal and Gwen sign-in (all public in instruction.md); constraints needs a saved M-11 post visible to Harriet in another context. Sequential shared-DB hazards checked against seed: timer_changes cutting M-13 to 7 days correctly deletes K-13/K-18 but leaves K-8 'Draft will sent for your review.' (2026-05-10, used later by message_links/live_updates) and the held K-7, so correct earlier behaviour does not break later criteria; earlier-criterion failures only cascade against the worse app. Replay refusals are paired with successes and the 'plain not available' bar is public (walls-and-retention.md:17); wall_every_route leg 5 explicitly accepts either valid JUDGE-W3 outcome. Residual, non-inverting observations: floor 0.05 > 1.5/44 and 2.0/44, so an app passing only one 1.5/2.0 criterion scores 0 (template policy, monotone); bundled conjunctive criteria are coarse (e.g., one wildcard bug forfeits all 4.0 of search_and_transcript) and timer_changes' earlier-versions leg applies only when a viewer exists (an app that leaks deleted versions through its viewer loses 4.0 while an app with no viewer loses edits 3.0 instead) - the leak is a real public retention violation, so this is not an inversion. Missing measurement (risk=true): raw-evidence-index scope states reward discrimination/ranking on these bytes is absent. Only hosted runs of PREVIOUS v2 bytes exist (Oracle 0.9917 > openhands/GPT-5.6 0.8114 > nop 0.0, hashes verified); v3 changed functional legs and three polish rows, so ordering on the current candidate is unmeasured and no mutated weak-app ranking record exists.
